The diagram above shows a unit circle. Rounding to two significant figures, the $x$-coordinate of the point $P$ is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14222207/assets/eba7dd6d571c989a14900a91eb432a216b74717046bfaa19e5fbe4de7abe6503.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $\theta ={20}^{∘}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡{20}^{∘}=0.939\,69…≈0.94.
$$
